title: Google gives Gemini a job: one agent that plans the work, gets its own work account, and reports back
summary: At a Google Cloud event on Thursday, October 8, Google launched a unified Gemini agent that can be handed “objectives, not just instructions,” as Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian put it: it plans the work, uses custom skills and tools, and connects to a company’s systems, from Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, and Slack to Jira, BigQuery, Snowflake, and any Model Context Protocol server, TechCrunch reports. It picks the best model by default, but users can choose another, starting with Anthropic’s Claude. The agent gets its own Workspace account and email address, knows who is on which team, their time zones and calendars, can be tagged, emailed, or added to a group chat, and writes an audit trail in its own name; a “tasks inbox” shows its thinking, subagents, and progress. Google is starting with businesses before consumers. Sundar Pichai said Gemini has more than 1 billion monthly active users and that nearly 90% of Fortune 100 companies use Gemini Enterprise; early testers included On, Shopify, and PayPal. Google also added cost controls such as smart routing and real-time spend caps.

title: OpenAI reportedly tells investors its revenue run rate is near $50 billion, about $20 billion below what had circulated
summary: The Financial Times reported October 8 that OpenAI has told investors its annualized revenue is “approaching $50 billion,” TechCrunch writes, roughly $20 billion below the nearly $70 billion figure reported a little over a week earlier. Per the FT, the higher number grew out of “attempts by OpenAI’s own investors to produce a direct comparison with Anthropic’s annualised revenues”; Anthropic counts sales made by its cloud partners in its annualized revenue, and OpenAI does not. TechCrunch notes that OpenAI raised $122 billion in a March funding round alone, that leaked 2025 financials showed about $13 billion in revenue against significantly more spending, and that its IPO, once rumored for this year, has been pushed to early 2027. TechCrunch said it had asked OpenAI for comment. The stocks desk below covers how chipmakers reacted.

title: USA Today and its local papers sue OpenAI, seeking more than $250 million
summary: USA Today Co., together with local newspapers it owns, including The Tennessean, IndyStar, The Columbus Dispatch, and The Oklahoman, sued OpenAI on Thursday, claiming the company copied “hundreds of thousands” of articles to train its AI models, The Verge reports, following Reuters. The filing asks for damages of more than $250 million and says OpenAI’s unauthorized use of its content “has done real and continuing” harm to its outlets. “OpenAI’s commercial success rests on large-scale copyright infringement,” the suit claims, alleging OpenAI never asked permission. It joins copyright cases against OpenAI from The New York Times, The Intercept, Ziff Davis, CBC/Radio-Canada, Encyclopaedia Britannica, Merriam-Webster, The Seattle Times, and a coalition of nearly 400 local newspapers. OpenAI didn’t immediately respond to The Verge. These are allegations; no court has ruled on them.

title: S&P 500 slips a second day as an OpenAI revenue report pulls the Nasdaq down 1.25%
summary: The S&P 500 lost 36.41 points, or 0.47%, to 7,765.36 on Thursday, its second straight decline after record closes earlier in the week, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 345.35 points, or 1.25%, to 27,193.34, Invested Alpha reports; the Dow edged up 51.77 points, or 0.10%, to 51,231.64. Technology was the worst of the 11 S&P 500 sectors and energy the best, as West Texas Intermediate crude settled $3.21 higher at $91.49 a barrel on Iran-related headlines. The 10-year Treasury yield eased to about 5.23% after a solid $22 billion 30-year auction, even as Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he anticipates additional rate hikes. Still ahead: the September consumer price index on October 14 and the Fed’s October 27–28 meeting. GROKI does not print live share prices.

title: Nvidia and the chipmakers slide as the AI trade digests a smaller OpenAI number
summary: Shares of Nvidia, Oracle, and CoreWeave fell Thursday after OpenAI told investors its annualized revenue was about $50 billion as of late September, short of the widely cited $68 billion, Quartz reports, citing CNBC; Oracle dropped more than 5%. Per Invested Alpha, citing Reuters, chipmakers fell 3.4% on the day after gaining more than 80% this year: Nvidia lost 2.9%, Advanced Micro Devices 3.9%, and Micron 4.8%. A person familiar with the matter told CNBC the gap doesn’t reflect lost sales; the higher figure included partners’ gross revenue to line OpenAI up against Anthropic, and OpenAI’s investor presentation showed 77% run-rate growth in the third quarter and 107% in its enterprise segment. Invested Alpha frames Friday’s question as whether this was a one-day repricing or the start of something larger. GROKI does not print live share prices.

title: StepFun’s Step 5 Preview: a 600-billion-parameter agent model, with open weights due October 15
summary: StepFun released Step 5 Preview, its new flagship model for agentic work, on October 8, according to OpenRouter’s listing. It is a sparse mixture-of-experts model with 600 billion total parameters and 27 billion active per token, a 1-million-token context window, and vision input, and StepFun says the open weights will be released October 15. In StepFun’s own benchmarks it scores 67.7% on DeepSWE v1.1, just ahead of Kimi K3 and GLM-5.3 but behind GPT-6 Astra at 74.1% and Claude Opus 5 at 74.0%. Given 24 hours to optimize a GPU kernel, it reached 508 TFLOPS versus 493 for Claude Opus 5, StepFun says, and a Pokémon Red run has passed 3,000 turns and three Gym Badges. OpenRouter lists it at $1 per million input tokens and $2.70 per million output tokens.

title: Odyssey-3: one world model that works a robot arm, drives a car, flies a drone, and plays GTA V
summary: AI lab Odyssey announced Odyssey-3 on October 8, calling it its most powerful foundation world model: a system trained on a vast collection of visual observations that learns how the world behaves, so it can adapt to new tasks with relatively little extra experience. Odyssey says it has demonstrated the model in six domains: controlling robot arms, including recovery behaviors it wasn’t explicitly trained on; powering humanoid control policies developed with Flexion; driving autonomously on roads in India with a policy trained on about 20 hours of simulated driving data; generating environments where AI agents can act and learn; piloting drones indoors around obstacles; and playing Grand Theft Auto V, with early transfer to other games without extra training. “World models give physical agents a foundation of knowledge they can carry from one machine, environment, or task to another,” said CEO Oliver Cameron.

title: In a real clinic, 98 patients talked with Google’s AMIE before urgent visits, and no chat had to be stopped
summary: Researchers at Google and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center published a study in The Lancet on October 8 testing AMIE, Google’s research diagnostic chatbot, in BIDMC’s ambulatory primary care clinic. Ninety-eight patients consulted AMIE ahead of urgent care visits while supervising physicians monitored the conversations in real time, and not one had to be interrupted under predefined safety criteria. Clinicians said AMIE’s summaries helped them prepare for visits in 75% of cases and influenced their approach to care in more than half, and its differential diagnoses matched the doctors’ final diagnoses 90% of the time. Google calls it its first publication in The Lancet’s main journal, and says larger clinical trials are needed to assess patient-facing AI at scale.

title: AWS open-sources a Physical AI Toolchain to take robots from data to deployment
summary: Amazon Web Services launched an open-source Physical AI Toolchain on October 8 that packages AWS services and NVIDIA’s physical AI software into a single workflow, The Robot Report reports. It covers five steps, synthetic data generation, model training, simulation and validation, edge deployment, and continuous improvement, using Amazon SageMaker and AWS IoT Greengrass alongside NVIDIA’s Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, Isaac GR00T, and Cosmos; companies can use the pieces individually or end to end, and data from robots in the field flows back to the cloud to keep improving models. “We’re trying to make this easy button,” said AWS’s Sri Elaprolu, who said it draws on lessons from Amazon’s more than 1 million robots and stays hardware-neutral. He pointed to Japanese company Telexistence, which has deployed more than 300 humanoids in convenience stores.

title: Teachers in India got two hours a week back from an AI lesson planner, and spent it on hands-on learning
summary: Researchers at Cornell and Microsoft Research India evaluated Shiksha Copilot, an AI system that turns textbook material into grade-appropriate lesson plans in English and Kannada, with more than 1,000 fifth- to 10th-grade teachers in Karnataka, the Cornell Chronicle reported October 8. Curators check every plan, teachers customize them, and guardrails keep examples local, like dosas instead of pizza. Teachers said it saved them an average of two hours a week and let them swap lecturing for hands-on activities such as collecting local leaves with different vein patterns. “Usually, whenever someone comes with something new, it just adds to our workload, but this is a burden-releasing concept,” said a science teacher with 20 years of experience. About 30,000 teachers in Telangana are using it this year, and the researchers found tailoring a tool to local needs can be up to 80% of the work. Today’s move: hand one chore to AI, then spend the time you win on the hands-on part.

title: Festivals Acadiens et Créoles opens tonight in Girard Park with the cutting of the boudin
summary: The 52nd Festivals Acadiens et Créoles opens with the cutting of the boudin at 5 p.m. Friday, October 9, and runs through the weekend in Lafayette, Acadiana News First reports. This year’s theme is “Fusion,” and for the first time in years the festival brings back a stage at Girard Park, the same stage where Beausoleil first performed at the festival in 1976. A collaboration with the Smithsonian explores how Appalachian, Irish, blues, and old-time country music helped shape Cajun and Creole music, alongside food, crafts, art, and folk life. “If you know nothing about Cajun and Creole culture, you can come here one weekend of the year and completely immerse yourself,” said the festival’s Pat Mould. Lafayette Travel lists tonight’s Scène Ma Louisiane sets as Jourdan Thibodeaux et Les Rôdailleurs at 5 p.m. and Ruben Moreno’s Zydeco Re-Evolution at 7 p.m., and calls it a free festival.

title: Today at the Hilliard: the Revolution and Evolution symposium, with the Smithsonian
summary: Festivals Acadiens et Créoles’ pre-festival symposium is today, Friday, October 9, starting at 9 a.m. on the second floor of the Hilliard Art Museum, 710 East St. Mary Boulevard (the festival’s page lists a 4 p.m. finish in its heading and 5 p.m. in its program notes). The theme is “Revolution and Evolution: Celebrating 250 Years of Cultural Fusion on the Bayou,” from the Center for Louisiana Studies, the festival, the Smithsonian, and the Hilliard. Panels cover the Indigenous, African, and European currents that shaped South Louisiana, how radio and social media spread Cajun and Creole culture, Ralph Rinzler’s 1960s Louisiana recordings, how the music was recorded and shared with the world, and Louisiana’s role in the American Revolution, with speakers including Christine Balfa, Lt. Gen. Russel Honoré, Nick Spitzer, Herman Fuselier, and Floyd Soileau. Barry Ancelet shows rare 1976 Smithsonian festival footage at lunch, and the day closes with a reception for the Elemore Morgan Jr. exhibit.

title: Free Bach Lunch with Jason Harrington kicks off festival day downtown
summary: Downtown Lafayette’s free lunchtime concert, Bach Lunch, features Louisiana singer-songwriter Jason Harrington today, Friday, October 9, at Parc Sans Souci, 201 East Vermilion Street. Food vendors start selling at 11 a.m. and music runs from noon to 1 p.m.; organizers suggest bringing blankets and chairs to picnic, and bill it as a kickoff for festival activities. Harrington’s music blends Cajun and Creole traditions with storytelling in the spirit of Bob Dylan and John Prine. Metered street parking is free after 5 p.m. on weekdays and all day on weekends, and the Parc-Auto du Centre-Ville garage is at 121 East Vermilion.

title: Never-shown Elemore Morgan Jr. festival photos open at the Hilliard today
summary: A new Hilliard Art Museum exhibition of 23 photographs by Louisiana photographer Elemore Morgan Jr. opens today, October 9, and runs through December 19, The Advocate reports. Many have never been shown publicly and were printed posthumously from his original slides. They capture Cajun and Creole musicians at the Smithsonian’s 1976 Festival of American Folklife on the National Mall. The show was organized with the Smithsonian Folklife Festival, the Center for Louisiana Studies, and the Morgan family, and the festival’s symposium ends today with a gallery conversation and opening reception in the exhibit.

title: WWE Friday Night SmackDown is back at the Cajundome tonight, its first Lafayette stop in three years
summary: The Cajundome hosts WWE Friday Night SmackDown tonight, Friday, October 9, at 6:30 p.m., with doors at 5 p.m.; the arena bills it as SmackDown’s return to Lafayette for the first time in three years. The advertised card includes Undisputed WWE Champion Sami Zayn, CM Punk, Cody Rhodes, Randy Orton, WWE Women’s Champion Chelsea Green, Gunther, Kevin Owens, United States Champion Trick Williams, and Damian Priest, with talent subject to change. Tickets are mobile-only Ticketmaster SafeTix, so screenshots and printouts won’t scan; the arena is cashless and enforces a clear-bag policy. Free parking is at the Congress Street Gate 8 entrance, with overflow at Cajun Field Gates 4 and 5. The Cajundome is at 444 Cajundome Blvd.; box office 337-265-2104.

title: Parc de Oaks opens its pumpkin patch on Moss Street this weekend
summary: Parc de Oaks, 3302 Moss Street, runs its pumpkin patch this weekend, October 9–11, and again October 16–18 and 23–25, according to The Lafayette Mom’s Acadiana pumpkin patch guide, which calls it the venue’s biggest event of the year, with food trucks, pumpkin picking and painting, kids’ activities, photo ops, and face painting. The guide lists the times as to be announced; Parc de Oaks’ own listing for its second weekend gives hours of 4 to 7 p.m. Friday and 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. Saturday and Sunday, free entry, pumpkin painting on Saturday and Sunday only, and limited parking, so carpool if you can. Check the venue’s page for this weekend’s exact times before you go.

title: October ArtWalk fills downtown’s galleries and studios Saturday night
summary: Downtown Lafayette’s monthly ArtWalk is Saturday, October 10, from 5 to 9 p.m., rain or shine, across the downtown cultural district. Museums, independent galleries, studios, craft stores, and art houses each host their own events with local artists and performers, and Downtown Lafayette is partnering with Lafayette Arts & Fleas to highlight local talent. It lands the same weekend as Festivals Acadiens et Créoles in Girard Park. Metered street parking downtown is free all day on weekends, and the Parc-Auto du Centre-Ville garage at 121 East Vermilion has 530 spaces.

title: Saturday and Sunday at Girard Park: Steve Riley, Wayne Toups, BeauSoleil, and a Bayou Blues Band with Sonny Landreth
summary: Lafayette Travel’s posted schedule for Festivals Acadiens et Créoles fills Girard Park on Saturday and Sunday. Saturday’s Scène Ma Louisiane runs from Jimmy Breaux & Friends at 10 a.m. to Steve Riley and the Mamou Playboys at 6 p.m., Scène Mon Heritage closes with Chris Ardoin & NuStep Zydeko at 6:30 p.m., and Balfa Toujours plays the Salle De Danse at 4:45 p.m. Sunday opens with a French Mass at 9 a.m. in the Salle De Danse; Lost Bayou Ramblers play Scène Mon Heritage at 5 p.m., Wayne Toups & Friends close Scène Ma Louisiane at 6:30 p.m., and the new Scène 76 has BeauSoleil at 11:30 a.m. and a 4:30 p.m. Bayou Blues Band with Roddie Romero, Sonny Landreth, Michael Doucet, and more. There are also workshops at Scène Atelier, jam sessions, and French games and story time with Alliance Française de Lafayette at La Tente Louisianaise.
